protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: at 4744169aa013a7360449418d5bfef8845b2ff8b4 RestartAction resolves the prior execution's binding, then calls StartAction with a new connect.Request containing BindingId and UniqueTrackingId but no caller headers. StartAction calls auth.UserFromApiCall on that synthetic request; runAuthChain reads req.Header(), and an unresolved identity falls back to UserGuest. The original restricted caller can therefore execute under broader guest permissions, matching the published GitHub advisory and CVE.org record.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CONFIRMED: git log -L over RestartAction and the parent-to-child diff identify 4744169aa013a7360449418d5bfef8845b2ff8b4 as the smallest first-write that replaces the nonfunctional FIXME with BindingId: execReqLogEntry.GetBindingId(). The change makes the already-headerless internal StartAction call resolve a real action; it is a one-parent commit, not a move, revert, merge, or release aggregate.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED: immediate parent e9a3863b1b9da97ce9377e8f6e87f3fc90de7449 is present and directly inspected. Its synthetic StartActionRequest leaves protobuf BindingId empty. StartAction first calls FindBindingByID("") and returns CodeNotFound when nil; registered binding IDs are an explicit nonempty action ID or a SHA-256 hex digest. The exploitable execution path is absent in the parent, so introducer_parent_absent=false is correct.
